intro: What each thing you sell really costs you, and what you keep from its price.
hidden: Your role doesn't show costs or margins. You can see names and prices.

how.title: How your costs are worked out
how.materials: Materials: the average of what you paid for them from {{from}} to {{to}}, or your last purchase.
how.askOwner: Ask the owner to set it in Settings.
how.noTime_one: {{count}} product has none of your time yet: add the minutes it takes you on the product.
how.noTime_other: {{count}} products have none of your time yet: add the minutes each takes you on the product.

rate.rule: Every {{one}} you spend on materials adds {{rate}} of running costs ({{percent}} of the materials).
rate.short: Running costs add {{percent}} to the cost of materials.

why.estimate: Why: your running costs are {{running}} a month and you buy about {{purchases}} of materials a month.
why.last_3_months: Why: your running costs are {{running}} a month and you bought {{purchases}} of materials a month on average from {{from}} to {{to}}.

rate.tooLarge: Your running costs are {{running}} a month and you buy about {{purchases}} of materials a month: too little to share them across.
rate.tooLarge_hidden: Your running costs are too large for what you buy in materials to share them across.
rate.not_set: Your running costs ({{running}} a month) aren't in your product costs yet: BizCost needs to know about how much you buy in materials a month.
rate.not_set_hidden: Your running costs aren't in your product costs yet: BizCost needs to know about how much you buy in materials a month.
rate.not_entered: You haven't entered your running costs yet (rent, electricity…), so your product costs don't include them.
rate.none: You have no running costs right now, so none are added to what you sell.
rate.noMaterials: Your running costs ({{running}} a month) aren't in your service costs yet: BizCost shares them by the materials each product uses, and your services use none. Sharing them by working time comes later.
rate.noMaterials_hidden: Your running costs aren't in your service costs yet: BizCost shares them by the materials each product uses, and your services use none. Sharing them by working time comes later.
rate.estimateUntil: BizCost uses your estimate until you have 3 full months of purchases: from {{date}}, it can use what you really bought.
rate.estimateUntilUnknown: BizCost uses your estimate until you have 3 full months of purchases, then what you really bought.
rate.estimateMonthsMissing: Some months from {{from}} to {{to}} have no purchases recorded, so BizCost uses your estimate. Once each of the last 3 full months has purchases, it uses what you really bought.
rate.estimateNothingBought: What you bought from {{from}} to {{to}} comes to nothing after returns, so BizCost uses your estimate.
rate.fromPurchases: You have 3 full months of purchases, so BizCost uses what you really bought.

time.rateNotSet: Your time: your hourly rate isn't set yet.

empty.title: Nothing to work out yet
empty.body: Add what you sell, and what each one costs you shows here.

noMatches.loss: Nothing here is sold at a loss.

short.no_recipe_service: No materials added (if it uses any)
short.unpriced_materials: Some materials have no price yet
short.unpriced_materials_food: Some ingredients have no price yet
short.unpriced_materials_retail: Some items have no price yet
short.running_costs_need_materials: No share of running costs yet: it uses no materials

long.no_recipe: Add what it uses, so the materials count.
long.no_recipe_food: Write its recipe, so its ingredients count.
long.no_recipe_retail: Add the items it uses, so they count.
long.no_recipe_service: If it uses materials, add them, so they count.
long.unpriced_materials: Some of what it uses was never bought, so it has no price yet. It counts once you buy it.
long.unpriced_named: Never bought, so no price yet: {{names}}. It counts once you buy it.
long.running_costs_not_entered: Enter your running costs (rent, electricity…), so a share of them is added to it.
long.running_costs_not_set: Your running costs aren't in it yet: tell BizCost about how much you buy in materials a month.
long.running_costs_need_materials: BizCost shares your running costs by the materials each product uses. This one uses none, so it carries no running costs for now. Sharing them by working time comes later.
long.hourly_rate_not_set: It has your minutes, but your hourly rate isn't set yet.
long.nothing_counted: Nothing of its cost is known yet.

detail.intro: What it really costs you {{per}}, part by part.
detail.atMost: At most {{percent}} of the price before VAT
detail.marginAtMost: The real margin is lower until what's missing is added.
detail.atPriceBeforeVat: At your price of {{price}}, which is {{beforeVat}} before VAT.
detail.noPrice: It has no price yet, so there's no margin. Set its usual price on the product.
detail.incomplete: This cost is incomplete: see what's missing.

lines.title: What its cost is made of
lines.resaleHint: The average of what you paid for it.
lines.whole: All the materials cost {{total}} and make {{qty}}.
lines.whole_food: The whole recipe costs {{total}} and makes {{qty}}.
lines.whole_retail: All the items cost {{total}} and make {{qty}}.
lines.withoutUnpriced: Without what has no price yet.
lines.runningShare: Its materials cost {{materials}}, so {{share}} of running costs is added to it.
lines.runningWaiting: Worked out once its materials have a price.
lines.runningNoRecipe: Worked out once what it uses is in.
lines.runningNoRecipe_food: Worked out once its recipe is in.
lines.runningNoRecipe_retail: Worked out once its items are in.
lines.timeNone: No time added for it. Add the minutes it takes you on the product.
lines.timeRateNotSet: {{minutes}}, but your hourly rate isn't set yet.

materials.basis: Average costs come from your purchases from {{from}} to {{to}}, or your last purchase for anything you didn't buy then. Shown rounded; BizCost keeps the exact amounts.

notFound.title: This product isn't here
notFound.body: It may have been removed, or the link is wrong.
